title: Physics-Informed Fractional Load Forecasting With Memory-Aware Break Detection for Reserve Scheduling (arXiv abstract)
note: Single author (A. Nikseresht), v1 only, 15 Nov 2026, eess.SY. Day-ahead load model: fractional temperature kernel for building thermal inertia, breaks and long memory estimated jointly, cone program for reserves. MAPE 15.7% (New England) and 10.3% (Mid-Atlantic) below the best of ten benchmarks. Reserve energy-limit breaches on 4.1% and 8.5% of days. No code or data link on the page.

title: Physics-informed fractional load paper, full text: data and protocol
note: ISO-NE hourly system load Mar 2003 to Apr 2017 (GEFCom2017 files); PJM hourly load Jan 2017 to Nov 2021 from an open dataset by Ruan et al., three weather stations; PJM coverage (RTO or zone) not stated. Issued 10:00 on D-1 for the 24 hours of day D (leads 15 to 38 h). Day-D temperatures are observed, not forecast. Tests: ISO-NE 2008-2016 (3,288 days), PJM 2019-2021 (1,065 days). Yearly refit.

title: Physics-informed fractional load paper, full text: accuracy results
note: MAPE: ISO-NE 1.56% vs 1.85% for the best benchmark (LSTM); PJM 2.13% vs 2.38% (GBDT with load lags). Other PJM benchmarks: MLP and LSTM 2.44, patch transformer 2.63, GBDT 2.91, KAN 2.94, adaptive GAM 3.21, recency MLR 3.64, vanilla MLR 4.45, APLF 5.45. LSTM is better in PJM 2019. 90% interval coverage 91.9% and 91.6%. No interval on the MAPE gain; DM tests are on squared errors.

title: Physics-informed fractional load paper, full text: benchmark inputs, reserves, limits
note: All methods are said to share one information set incl. observed day-D temperature; the proposed model uses no load lags. No foundation model tested. Reserve study: breach days 4.1%/8.5% with the joint error covariance vs 36.7%/57.5% with a diagonal one. Limits named: observed temperatures, breaks only in level and thermal sensitivity. PJM breach rate 8.5% exceeds the expected 5.3%.

title: Physics-informed fractional load paper, full text: availability
note: No code, repository or software statement; no pre-registration. Runtime about 3 to 4 minutes per test year on an 8-core Xeon with 12 GB RAM. The last 21,573 characters (supplement proofs) were read separately and hold no availability statement; the reference list and supplementary Table SII (per-year MAPE) were not seen. The PDF fetch returned no readable text.
